Name: cmcc-core-r0
Description: The runnable companion to the CMCC-Core Representation Theorem, retrofitted into ERB shape: the R0 warehouse-network spec's own structure, its conformance matrix (answer key x reflection), and the resulting per-substrate roll-ups, all as rulebook data.

EDBRelations.Description: The R0 spec's extensional database relations (r0/spec.json's 'edb' map): the fixed vocabulary every rule and command is built from.

schema.name: RelationId
schema.Description: Stored identity: the EDB relation name from r0/spec.json's edb map (e.g. 'Warehouse').

schema.name: Fields
schema.Description: JSON array of the relation's field names, verbatim from spec.json (e.g. '["id"]').

schema.name: FieldCount
schema.Description: Number of fields, counted once at transcription time.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this EDB relation models in the warehouse-network domain.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: SeedFacts
schema.Description: h0 seed facts whose Relation is this EDB relation.

schema.name: TransitionEffects
schema.Description: Transition effects that assert/retract into this relation.

data.Description: A node in the network (the hub, satellite depots, or ordinary warehouses).
A directed shipping lane between two warehouses with a capacity.
A shipment currently sitting at a warehouse on a given day.

Commands.Description: The R0 spec's commands (r0/spec.json's 'commands' map): the only way an input history can act on the state.

schema.name: CommandId
schema.Description: Stored identity: the command name from r0/spec.json's commands map (e.g. 'AddRoute').

schema.name: Params
schema.Description: JSON array of the command's parameter names, verbatim from spec.json.

schema.name: ParamCount
schema.Description: Number of parameters, counted once at transcription time.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What issuing this command means in the warehouse-network domain.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Transitions
schema.Description: Transitions this command can fire.

data.Description: Open a new directed route s -> d with capacity c.
Close (retract) an existing route s -> d.
Bitemporal correction: retract the recorded day for a shipment and re-assert a new day, both visible at knowledge time 'at'.
Ask that a warehouse gain a fallback route, either via the hub or via the depot (two enabled transitions -> nondeterminism).
A no-op command that only emits an observation tag; asserts and retracts nothing.

Rules.Description: Every stratified Datalog-with-negation-and-aggregation rule in the R0 spec (r0/spec.json's 'rules' array), including guard/effect/event rules for transitions and the two integrity-constraint rules.

schema.name: RuleId
schema.Description: Stored identity: the rule's 'id' in r0/spec.json's rules array (e.g. 'reach_base').

schema.name: HeadPredicate
schema.Description: The rule's head predicate name (head[0] in spec.json), e.g. 'Reachable'.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: 'rule' for a body-clause rule, 'aggregation' for an agg-clause rule (spec.json's 'agg' key).

schema.name: HeadJson
schema.Description: The rule's head tuple, verbatim JSON from spec.json.

schema.name: BodyJson
schema.Description: The rule's body clause list, verbatim JSON from spec.json (null for aggregation rules).

schema.name: AggJson
schema.Description: The rule's agg clause, verbatim JSON from spec.json (null for body rules).

schema.name: PaperSectionRef
schema.Description: CMCC-Core Representation Theorem section(s) this rule exercises.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What the rule computes and, for reflection.py, which G_R node it constructs.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: GuardedTransitions
schema.Description: Transitions whose Guard is this rule.

schema.name: TransitionEffects
schema.Description: Transition effects whose FromRule is this rule.

schema.name: TransitionEvents
schema.Description: Transition events whose FromRule is this rule.

schema.name: IntegrityConstraints
schema.Description: Integrity constraints whose Rule is this rule.

data.Description: Base case of positive recursion: a direct route makes y reachable from x.
Recursive step of positive recursion: Reachable composes with one more Route hop.
Negation over a strictly lower stratum: a warehouse not reachable from the hub.
COUNT aggregation: out-degree of a warehouse; the empty group gives 0.
MAX aggregation: largest outgoing route capacity; the empty group derives nothing.
Comparison over an aggregation result: warehouses whose MaxCap is at least 50.
A 'let' binding: DoubleCap re-derives a value via arithmetic, not just projection.
Comparison over an EDB field: shipments recorded past day 10.
Reads Hist_Shipment at a given knowledge time k, exercising the bitemporal snapshot rules tau generates.
Guard for AddRoute: both endpoints exist and no route already connects them.
Effect for AddRoute: the asserted Route tuple, valid from now to +inf.
Event for AddRoute: emits RouteAdded.
Guard for CloseRoute: the route currently exists.
Effect for CloseRoute: retracts the live Hist_Route tuple for s -> d.
Guard for CorrectShipment: the shipment currently exists.
Retract half of the correction: the live Hist_Shipment tuple for this shipment.
Assert half of the correction: the new day, valid from the given knowledge time 'at'.
Event for CorrectShipment: emits ShipmentCorrected.
Guard for RerouteViaHub: enabled whenever x has no route to the hub.
Effect for RerouteViaHub: asserts a route from x to the hub.
Guard for RerouteViaDepot: enabled whenever x has no route to the depot.
Effect for RerouteViaDepot: asserts a route from x to the depot.
Guard for Observe: always enabled when the command is issued.
Constraint: a route with negative capacity, which rejects the transition that would create it.
Constraint: a route from a warehouse to itself, which rejects the transition that would create it.

Transitions.Description: The R0 spec's transitions (r0/spec.json's 'transitions' array): command + guard pairs that may fire, each with its effects and events.

schema.name: TransitionId
schema.Description: Stored identity: the transition's 'name' in r0/spec.json's transitions array (e.g. 'AddRoute').

schema.name: Command
schema.Description: The command that can fire this transition.

schema.name: Guard
schema.Description: The rule whose head predicate gates this transition.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this transition does when its guard is satisfied.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: Effects
schema.Description: This transition's ordered assert/retract effects.

schema.name: Events
schema.Description: This transition's emitted events.

data.Description: Opens a new route; the sole enabled transition for command AddRoute.
Closes an existing route; the sole enabled transition for command CloseRoute.
Bitemporal correction of a shipment's recorded day: retracts the old fact and asserts the new one under one knowledge time.
One of two transitions enabled by command Reroute: adds a fallback route via the hub.
The other transition enabled by command Reroute: adds a fallback route via the depot. Together with RerouteViaHub this is the spec's one genuinely nondeterministic command (§20).
A no-op transition: enabled whenever Observe is issued, asserts and retracts nothing.

TransitionEffects.Description: One row per (transition, effect) pair: an ordered assert/retract of a rule's derived tuples into an EDB relation.

schema.name: EffectId
schema.Description: Stored identity: '<TransitionId>#effect<index>', ordered as in spec.json.

schema.name: Transition
schema.Description: The transition this effect belongs to.

schema.name: Op
schema.Description: 'assert' or 'retract'.

schema.name: Relation
schema.Description: The EDB relation this effect asserts into or retracts from.

schema.name: FromRule
schema.Description: The rule whose derived tuples this effect applies.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

TransitionEvents.Description: One row per (transition, event) pair: an event relation emitted when the transition fires.

schema.name: EventId
schema.Description: Stored identity: '<TransitionId>#event<index>', ordered as in spec.json.

schema.name: Transition
schema.Description: The transition this event belongs to.

schema.name: EventRelation
schema.Description: The event relation name emitted (e.g. 'RouteAdded'); not an EDB relation.

schema.name: FromRule

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

IntegrityConstraints.Description: The R0 spec's integrity constraints (r0/spec.json's 'constraints' array): predicates whose nonempty derivation rejects a transition. schema.name: Rule

schema.name: Name

data.Description: Rejects any transition whose effect would leave a route with negative capacity.
Rejects any transition whose effect would leave a route from a warehouse to itself.

data.Description: AddRoute/CloseRoute/Reroute traffic over the warehouse network; exercises recursion, negation, aggregation and the nondeterministic Reroute command.

ReflectionConditions.Description: The six conditions of constructor reflection, section 13 of the paper.

schema.name: ConditionId
schema.Description: Stored identity, matching conformance/matrix.json's condition keys (e.g. '1_constructor_preservation').

schema.name: ConditionNumber
schema.Description: The condition's number in §13 (1-6).

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Short name of the condition.

schema.name: PaperSectionRef
schema.Description: Paper section this condition is defined in.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What the condition checks on the substrate artifact's call graph.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: ReflectionResults
schema.Description: Per-substrate pass/fail/delegated outcomes for this condition.

data.Title: Constructor preservation
data.Description: Every G_R node has a function of its kind in the artifact.

data.Title: Dependency preservation
data.Description: Every source edge in G_R is a call edge in the artifact.

data.Title: Addressability
data.Description: Every G_R node has an image (a named function) in the artifact.

data.Title: Local adequacy
data.Description: Delegated to the answer key by design (§13); this condition is always recorded as delegated, never pass/fail.

data.Title: Injectivity
data.Description: Distinct G_R nodes map to distinct functions.

data.Title: Bounded locality
data.Description: No public function that is not an image; no call between images that is not a source edge; no run-time name resolution.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this substrate is and how it is generated.

schema.name: PaperSectionRef
schema.Description: Paper section(s) this substrate demonstrates.

schema.name: IsControl
schema.Description: True for the two substrates that are deliberately expected to fail reflection (tangled, interpreter).

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias.

schema.name: AnswerKeyResults
schema.Description: This substrate's per-input-history answer-key results.

schema.name: ReflectionResults
schema.Description: This substrate's per-condition reflection results.

schema.name: AnswerKeyResultCount
schema.Description: Number of answer-key results recorded for this substrate.

schema.name: AnswerKeyFailCount
schema.Description: Number of answer-key results recorded as a failure for this substrate.

schema.name: AnswerKeyOk
schema.Description: True when every recorded answer-key result for this substrate passed (§11).

schema.name: ReflectionResultCount
schema.Description: Number of reflection results recorded for this substrate.

schema.name: ReflectionFailCount
schema.Description: Number of reflection conditions recorded as a failure for this substrate.

schema.name: ReflectionOk
schema.Description: True when no recorded reflection condition failed for this substrate (§13). Delegated conditions never count as a failure.

schema.name: Conformant
schema.Description: True only when this substrate passes both gates: the answer key and reflection.

data.Description: transpile.py emits one function per G_R node: a rule body as explicit nested loops, a non-recursive predicate as the union of its rules, a recursive stratum as a c_mu_* fixed-point driver. runtime.py never reads the spec JSON.

The transparent module with every predicate read inside a rule routed through _dispatch(name, S), which resolves the target by name at run time. Same computation, same answers; dependency preservation and bounded locality fail because dependencies are now strings resolved dynamically.

The rulebook loaded as inert JSON and handed to one universal evaluator (the SQLite oracle, compiling at request time). Zero image functions; constructor preservation, dependency preservation and addressability all fail.

schema.name: Outcome

data.StringValue: The CMCC-Core Representation Theorem, made runnable: two gates, three substrates, one divergence.

Runnable companion to the CMCC-Core Representation Theorem paper. An R0 warehouse-network spec is checked two ways -- an answer key (adequacy, section 11) and reflection (structural transparency, section 13) -- across three substrates. All three pass the answer key; only the transparent substrate passes reflection. This rulebook models the spec's own structure (relations, rules, transitions, constraints, observables, seed facts) and the conformance matrix as first-class data; it does not re-implement R0's stratified Datalog semantics, which stays the exclusive job of the reference evaluator and the SQLite oracle.

Direction of truth: r0/spec.json is transcribed into EDBRelations/Commands/Rules/Transitions/.../SeedFacts as static structural data (a mirror, not a computation). conformance/matrix.json -- produced fresh by conformance/run.py from the reference evaluator and the independent SQLite oracle -- is ingested into AnswerKeyResults and ReflectionResults. Substrates.AnswerKeyOk / ReflectionOk / Conformant are the one legitimate rulebook computation here: an AND/COUNT rollup of those already-witnessed rows, never a re-derivation of R0 semantics itself.
CMCC-Core Representation Theorem (section references throughout this rulebook are to that paper).
